screening_population: healthy full- and post-term newborns; normal routine clinical examination
screening_algorithm_raw: postductal foot SpO2; >=96% pass; <=95% repeated after 1 h; persistent <=95% = positive; positive followed by clinical examination and echocardiography
study_target_definition_raw: all forms of critical CHD for which early surgical or catheter intervention is mandatory for survival
individual_diagnoses: persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn; sepsis; healthy
management_actionability_evidence: The primary report identifies 15 PPHN and 13 sepsis among CCHD-negative final failed screens, but does not report treatment, disposition, escalation, or diagnosis-specific follow-up for those 28 infants. Earlier diagnosis is discussed as potentially beneficial, not as documented individual management.
poolability_reason: all 40 CCHD-negative final failed screens are clinically classified; 28 clinically relevant diagnoses lack qualifying actionability evidence and therefore map to CAN-U under the locked protocol
source_full_text_provenance: Primary full text: Riede FT et al. Eur J Pediatr. 2010;169:975-981. PMID 20195633; PMCID PMC2890074; DOI 10.1007/s00431-010-1160-4
extraction_notes: Strict CAN-CCHD 0/40; Expanded CAN-CCHD 28/40; explicitly healthy 12/40. This intentionally differs from any diagnosis-as-actionable shorthand.

screening_algorithm_raw: pre- and postductal pulse oximetry with protocol-defined repeat sequence; persistent positive underwent echocardiographic/clinical evaluation
study_target_definition_raw: critical congenital heart disease; three screen-positive lesions were TGA with intact ventricular septum x2 and pulmonary atresia x1
diagnosis_categories_raw: early-onset sepsis/congenital pneumonia; PPHN; transitional circulation
diagnosis_counts_raw: early-onset sepsis/congenital pneumonia 8; PPHN 2; transitional circulation 3
individual_diagnoses: early-onset sepsis/congenital pneumonia; persistent pulmonary hypertension; transitional circulation
management_actionability_evidence: Primary text states that false-positive screens picked up early-onset sepsis/congenital pneumonia, PPHN and transitional circulation and that these were 'managed as per standard guidelines'. The source does not specify the concrete treatment, escalation, disposition, or follow-up for the 10 disease cases. Under the locked Protocol Core this is insufficient for Strict actionability, so those 10 map to CAN-U; transitional circulation remains NON_CAN.
poolability_reason: denominator and diagnoses are fully classified; the locked CAN-U category resolves clinically relevant disease without specific documented actionability rather than requiring a hold
source_full_text_provenance: Primary full text: Gopalakrishnan S et al. Med J Armed Forces India. 2021;77:214-219. PMCID PMC8042503; DOI 10.1016/j.mjafi.2020.01.007
extraction_notes: Strict CAN-CCHD 0/13; Expanded CAN-CCHD 10/13; NON_CAN/transitional 3/13. Generic 'managed as per standard guidelines' is preserved but does not satisfy the specific-actionability threshold.

site_program: Brigham and Women's Hospital, Boston, Massachusetts
screening_population: newborns >=35 weeks cared for in well-infant nursery
screening_algorithm_raw: three-stage pulse-oximetry screening; 35 failed first screen, 34 passed subsequent screening, one failed all 3 and underwent echocardiography
study_target_definition_raw: CCHD screening in a tertiary-care nursery with very high prenatal detection
management_actionability_evidence: The only final failed screen triggered echocardiography showing PPHN. Accessible primary report does not document treatment, escalation, disposition change, or diagnosis-specific follow-up attributable to PPHN; echocardiography is diagnostic ascertainment and is not itself counted as actionability.
poolability_reason: complete diagnosis ascertainment; clinically relevant PPHN lacks qualifying actionability evidence and maps to CAN-U
source_full_text_provenance: Primary article/abstract: Johnson LC et al. Pediatrics. 2014;134:916-922. PMID 25287457; DOI 10.1542/peds.2014-1461

screening_population: babies born at home and screened by attending midwife
screening_algorithm_raw: routine homebirth pulse-oximetry protocol; published peer-reviewed report describes two positive screens
individual_diagnoses: significant respiratory illness requiring neonatal-unit admission
management_actionability_evidence: Both positive-screen infants were admitted to the neonatal unit with significant respiratory illness. The diagnosis category and acute escalation/disposition are both explicitly supported by the primary report.
poolability_reason: complete diagnosis and actionability ascertainment; 100% ascertainment
source_full_text_provenance: Primary peer-reviewed report: Cawsey MJ et al. Arch Dis Child Fetal Neonatal Ed. 2016;101:F349-F351. PMID 26915671; DOI 10.1136/archdischild-2015-309936
extraction_notes: Strict CAN-CCHD 2/2; early-screen/out-of-hospital setting retained for heterogeneity analyses.
